accuracy.evidence: Checked against NC 2013 Year 4 Sound ('recognise that vibrations from sounds travel through a medium to the ear') and its non-statutory guidance (string telephones, sound in different materials), and speed values from Kaye and Laby / NPL tables: air 343 m/s at 20 °C, fresh water about 1,480 m/s, steel about 5,960 m/s (longitudinal). Lab times recomputed: 100/343 = 0.29 s, 100/1480 = 0.068 s, 100/5960 = 0.017 s; thunder about 3 s per km (1000/343 = 2.9). The bell jar meter keeps a 5% floor and the text says 'almost', since a real pump never reaches a perfect vacuum and some sound leaks through the base. Helmet-to-helmet talking in a vacuum is the documented conduction effect. The 'solids are fastest' reason is phrased as 'packed close and held tightly' (stiffness), not 'closer particles' alone.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented sound misconceptions (Eshach and Schwartz 2006, 'Sound stuff? Naive materialism in middle-school students' conceptions of sound', IJSE 28(7); Linder 1993; Hrepic, Zollman and Rebello 2010): sound as stuff or air that travels to the ear (prediction 2, 'travel', p5), sound only in air ('aironly', p1), sound travelling more freely in space ('space', 'quiet', m7), the lightest medium being fastest (prediction 1, 'light'), and walls blocking sound ('gaps', 'make', m1).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagmedium is about the medium itself: the same drum through air, water and steel particle rows with timed arrival, one tracked particle that returns to its tick mark, a string telephone that works only tight and unpinched, a bell jar with an air pump and sound meter, and two astronauts who can only talk when helmets touch. flagvib is about what vibrates, flagloud about loud and quiet, flagpitch about high and low. Max 6-shingle similarity 2.2% (flag_balf.js); explanation overlap 0.2% (The particle model).

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner finds each idea by doing: the timings appear as each material is tried (air 0.29 s, water 0.068 s, steel 0.017 s), the red particle visibly jiggles and settles on its mark, the slack string fades the pulse and the pinch stops it, the sound meter drops as air dots vanish while the hammer still hits, and Ana's voice reaches Ben only when helmets touch.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options disproved on screen: 'air, it is the lightest' (air is slowest), 'yes, it carries the sound to the ear' (the red particle stays), 'nothing changes' when pinched (the pulse stops at the pinch), plus a fourth on the bell jar where 'the same ring' is disproved by the meter.

challenge_feedback.evidence: slip() has 10 distinct messages (gaps, make, aironly, quiet, space, air, travel, light, mid, still), each naming the specific wrong idea, e.g. 'Nothing blocks it, but nothing carries it either. Sound needs a material.' and 'Not the lightest. Sound is slowest in air, where particles are far apart.' In-lab feedback names why a slack or pinched string fails.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes for the family audience: kid FK 1.8, adult FK 9.5. Kid text uses shake, vibrate, travel, jiggle, bump, with everyday examples (wall, swimming, space); 'medium' and speeds in m/s are kept for the adult panel.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (no banned phrases; explanation overlap under 1% with every lesson). Kid paragraphs: vibration to ear; passing it on; fastest in solids with examples; no sound in space. Adult paragraphs: standard and key words; particle explanation with speeds; named mistakes; what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots after Show me on every step at 360 px Android in light and dark, plus mid-step string-telephone and bell-jar views: the timing strip, particle row, ear, cups, pinch marker, sound meter, pump and astronauts fit; the ear was moved in from the right edge and the pump label given full text colour after the first screenshots; buttons wrap below the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has a button twin ('Push the drum skin', 'Pull the string tight', 'Pinch the string', 'Pump some air out of the jar', 'Move Ana closer'). The canvas aria-label and narration update after each action and each arrival. walk.cjs: desktop and iPhone 13 complete all 5 tasks with Show me, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes, no console errors.
